# Independent table type-erasure source review

The proposed main-line `do-not-adopt` source decision for `dabbf3e97b65f06832995b217f3c680d89675515` is supported, within the packet's source-only scope. Patch SHA-256 `9f800b4c41805062d8d7692a6de31a2a8e4f3f4be24276068533b86aa3c0782c`; manifest SHA-256 `b1611124d76b053752f9a6cdd4c00c415d2416d39265c5861189c4c3563c54f5`. Strict whitespace apply-check passed against both declared base `4c29be143432bcb5b2ca99d4f83ca6ff162b4554` and the current checked HEAD. The declared-base ledger afterimage changes exactly one of 1697 rows, retaining the full prior inherited row and its prior evidence reference.

The actual single-parent upstream change has exactly 15 paired changes across three files: one production `filteredData!: T[]` assertion and 14 test-fixture property assertions. Every changed line differs only by the definite-assignment `!`; no initializer, runtime statement, template or style changed. The embedded full-index diff matches exact Git-object-cache output, SHA-256 `6ea94991e1d0eab0b018ad13d88faf61764e11decf75b9b070dd07b03ae0339b`. Independent TypeScript 6.0.3 `transpileModule` comparisons of all three complete before/after files were byte-identical for ES2020 and ES2022 under both class-field-definition settings, 12 comparisons. This is not an Angular AOT, declaration-compatibility or runtime test.

The legacy public data-source class extends an owned `_MatTableDataSource`; the presence of peer Material table **testing harness** imports does not imply the production data source inherits the modern peer implementation. Current source and the seven declared evidence references matched their hashes. The new source-only record explicitly says execution is not claimed; the old inherited entry remains in the preserved prior record rather than being silently rewritten as runtime proof.

An independent isolated run of the actual b6ef production checker with the exact proposed row and its original evidence path reported zero missing-evidence, individual-proof and branch failures for the subject. Separate actual-dispatch cases rejected wrong branch, stale source hash, unknown kind, conflicting review decision, wrong SHA, false runtime claim and tampered upstream diff. The overall checker process still returned nonzero for unrelated aggregate requirements. The author's separately recorded full-ledger comparison reports removal of this SHA from individual and branch insufficiencies and a lower inherited count due to its changed disposition; I did not independently repeat that full-ledger comparison. Hash validation and a consistent written decision do not establish semantic truth; the independent full-diff/source inspection above supplies the bounded substantive review. No browser, historical family, 21.x, security, G11 or release pass follows.

# Independent table type-erasure v2 transport review

The v2 patch fixes the v1 raw-ledger reserialization problem without changing the previously reviewed source evidence or tests. Patch SHA-256 `40036b30a9cd5525427947464d9eabdcabcabf25245dce5b208c039077f514a2`; manifest SHA-256 `a5eda9cdd2ba804ea33cf823ab136aae558bc8a1f1a8f527e5eac31799d4cc76`.

The first 4,621,645 bytes are exactly equal; predecessor bytes from offset 4,623,179 equal candidate bytes from offset 4,628,414 through EOF. Parsing confirms only SHA `dabbf3e97b65f06832995b217f3c680d89675515` changes among 1,697 entries and all top-level metadata remains equal. Its complete prior row is preserved in the review.

Strict `git apply --cached --check --whitespace=error-all` passes on the declared base and the checked current HEAD. The six evidence and test images extracted from independently applied v1 and v2 indexes are byte-identical and match both manifests. Thus the prior bounded semantic and targeted dispatcher review remains applicable; this check did not rerun those tests or claim fresh full-ledger qualification. The earlier v1 checker comparison used a semantically equal reserialized baseline; the reported root zero-test attempt remains a failure to establish any test pass.
